about: Lab scenarios for the console's Lab tab (BACKLOG B13). A wish is the game's own cheat prompt (Ctrl+W, or Shift+W for a menu; verified in Commands.xml). Use a throwaway character with the AI paused. Confidence per command: 'documented' = listed with a label in the game's WishCommands.xml; 'named' = the string is recognised by the engine's wish handler (Wishing.HandleWish) but what it does was not read; the human should say what each one really did.

scenarios.title: Turret nest
scenarios.why: Test the turret doctrine (HANDOFF issue 77) without waiting for a run that meets one: a turret listed as an enemy, shot with Lase, never rested in front of.
setup: Pause the AI. Walk to an open floor with about 6 tiles of clear line to the east.
Wish for the turrets below, step 4 to 5 tiles away so one has line of sight, then Engage the AI.

wishes.note: a musket turret (level 15, 5 HP); expected to appear next to you
a second one, for the two-turret retreat rule

watch: the turret in last_state.json with is_enemy true and max_hp 5
a Lase aimed at the turret, then the turret gone
no REST while it has line of sight

scenarios.title: Very Tough creature next to you
scenarios.why: Test the lethal adjacent guard (issue 75): Teleport Other, Force Bubble or Intimidate instead of Lase.
setup: Pause the AI. Use a character of level 3 to 5 with at least one of those abilities ready.
Wish for the creature, then Engage.

wishes.note: level 12, 45 HP; Very Tough for a level 3 to 5 character

watch: the creature gone or controlled on the first turn

scenarios.title: Proselytize odds by level gap
scenarios.why: Fill memory/proselytize_log.jsonl quickly (BACKLOG B11): attempts on calm creatures at known levels, with the 25-turn cooldown cleared between tries.
setup: Pause the AI. Wish for a calm creature next to you, Engage, wait for the [PROSELYTIZE] line, Pause, clear the cooldown, repeat.
watch: the report's rate per level gap

scenarios.title: Set the character's level
scenarios.why: Reach a level (to test a level-gated rule such as the dive gates) without grinding. The XP needed comes from the game's own curve (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.16); the tab computes how much to add from your current XP.
setup: Pause the AI. Pick the level in the tab; it shows the exact wish.

wishes.note: the game's own menu has 'Gain 25,000 XP' as xp:25000, so the amount after the colon is XP to add; level-ups still need to be taken (AP, SP, mutations) by the brain or by you

watch: the brain spending the new attribute and skill points

scenarios.title: Quiet walk (navigation and exits)
scenarios.why: Test exploration, exit and stairs logic (issues 71, 73, 74) without being killed halfway: calm creatures, or an invulnerable character.
setup: Pause the AI. Wish, then Engage and watch the Live actions tab.

wishes.note: 'Toggle godmode'; wish again to turn it off. Do not leave it on for a run you want to count

watch: USE_STAIRS_UP from a dead-end stratum, and no walk straight back down

scenarios.title: Give an item (trade and gear tests)
scenarios.why: Test the item scorer and inventory actions (issues 66, 72) and trade ideas (B8) with an item you name.
setup: Pause the AI. Wish for the item, then Engage and read the [INVENTORY] lines.

wishes.note: the game's menu spawns items with item:<Blueprint>; the blueprint names are in data/items.json
an item worth 200 base, for the sell side of a trade

watch: that a gifted firearm is kept (Test 93)

scenarios.title: Quest state (quest log tests)
scenarios.why: Check the quest log export and the [QUEST] lines (issue 76) for a quest you did not take by hand.
setup: Pause the AI. Wish, Engage for a few turns, open the Quests tab.

wishes.note: the quest name is the one in Quests.xml

wishes.cmd: finishqueststep:What's Eating the Watervine?~Travel to Red Rock
wishes.note: the step id format 'Quest~Step' appears in the game's conversations; the exact wish syntax was not read

watch: the quest in the Quests tab
a [QUEST] new quest or step finished line
